newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KPN clears decks for cable ops sale.
newsitem.headline: KPN clears decks for cable ops sale.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV (KPN) said on Wednesday its cable division Vision Networks had agreed to buy the outstanding shares in cable company Casema, bringing it up to 100 percent ownership.
KPN said in a statement the move gave the company more flexibility to carry out its previously announced intention to sell off all or part of its cable interests.

Vision Networks is to buy the 22.56 percent Casema stake owned by Dutch public broadcasting infrastructure company Nozema, and the 0.75 percent held together by public broadcasters AVRO, KRO and NCRV.

KPN said the deal, which was agreed in principle on Tuesday, would be carried out at the shares' book value, plus a premium which will depend on the price realised by KPN via any sale of its Casema interest.
"We currently have 76.69 percent of Casema and through this we would have 100 percent of the company," Vision Networks managing director Paul 't Hoen said in a telephone interview.
KPN has agreed with the Dutch government to cut its holding in Casema to a maximum 20 percent by July 1, 1998, as part of a deal for Casema to meet regional infrastructure licence requirements.

KPN was buying out the remaining shareholders to make it easier to sell off Casema, said 't Hoen. "There are a lot of complications that you have if you have to sell things that are not 100 percent owned," he said.

Canadian telephone company TELUS Corp said on Tuesday it planned to sell its 50 percent interest in British cable firm Telecential Communications to its partner Vision Networks for C$390 million, making Vision Networks 100 percent owner.
